concept: spoon-shaped figure in flooded art-deco transit mosaic conservation
negative_en: low resolution, warped walls, impossible perspective, cartoon style, fake-looking background, 3D render look, broken window geometry, illustration look, excessive HDR, over-processed retouching
prompt_en: Photorealistic full-length conservation editorial of one unmistakably adult woman in her late twenties or older in a shallowly flooded art-deco transit concourse. Fully clothed in smooth unpadded non-cinching matte waterproof coveralls, boots, gloves, and a slim utility belt, she stands in an eye-level normal-lens near-frontal three-quarter view. Her spoon high-hip silhouette relation is explicit: both high-hip regions remain visible in an adult bilateral waist-to-thigh silhouette; the natural waist is visibly located above the transition and remains distinct from the utility belt; a rapid outward projection at the high hip forms a shelf-like upper-hip transition below the waist; the high-hip projection continues into broad hips and thighs on both sides. Her upper torso stays narrower; a sharply defined waist flows into a pronounced high-hip shelf, broad rounded hips, and visibly fuller upper thighs. Her facial appearance—face shape, features, complexion, hairline, and hairstyle—takes its cue only from the attached image. In ankle-deep water, the conservator draws a low-pressure suction wand along one loosened tessera seam to remove flood silt. Wet geometric mosaics, brass arches, loose tesserae, abstract unlettered condition markers, and rippling cool-and-warm work-light reflections make the emergency conservation action credible.
